reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes StrongBlock as a passive crypto investment while claiming that viewers can recover their investment in about 3.6 months and earn thousands of dollars monthly. The creator also directs viewers to join a paid crypto investment group for access to recommended investments and claims a 100% money-back guarantee. The presentation is promotional rather than reporting or criticism, and it combines specific high-return claims with a direct solicitation for money.

opening.argument: The presentation uses approximate, conditional language rather than presenting a guaranteed financial outcome. The token price is described as “around 700 bucks” and “actually down right now,” and the speaker distinguishes his own position by saying, “personally, I have four nodes.” The payback calculation is therefore a personal estimate based on a fluctuating crypto price and stated assumptions, not an assurance that every viewer will receive the same result. That makes this investment commentary with acknowledged uncertainty, even if the presenter ultimately expresses enthusiasm.

citations.quote: Strong current price of strong is around 700 bucks. It's actually down right now.
So right now, personally, I have four nodes.
if i just do 28 000 divided by 7680 i make my money back in 3.64 months

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited figures are projections, but projection is not the same as deception. The speaker identifies an ongoing expense by explaining that viewers must pay node fees monthly, and the price itself is expressly described as currently falling. “Yes, absolutely” is an opinion about whether the arrangement is worthwhile, not proof that the underlying crypto asset is risk-free or that the estimate applies universally.

citations.quote: It's actually down right now.
back in there pay your node fees 20 bucks per note

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the price approximate does not meaningfully warn viewers that the projected return may fail. The presentation still foregrounds a concrete recovery period and describes the arrangement as passive. Mentioning a monthly fee identifies maintenance, but it does not disclose that the claimed income or token value is uncertain enough to defeat the advertised payback calculation.

being one of those type of crypto investments that is like 100% passive

opening.argument: The central activity is an operational demonstration of a calculator, not merely a demand that viewers send money. The speaker says he will share his screen and show “exactly the numbers,” then identifies an Excel sheet that generates the calculation. The sampled frames show a spreadsheet titled “STRONGcalc (BASIC),” with inputs and automatically generated outputs, and another calculator marked view-only with instructions to make a copy. This is a walkthrough of how to model node costs, output, and recovery time, which fits an educational technology or financial-tool demonstration.

citations.quote: So let me share my screen really quick and let me show you exactly the numbers behind this.
my buddy gave me a little Excel sheet that kind of generates it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A demonstration can still be promotional, but the evidence shows the speaker explaining a reproducible spreadsheet rather than hiding how the estimate is produced. The invitation to a separate group occurs after the calculator walkthrough and describes broader research services, including yield farms, staking, and other crypto topics. That later offer does not convert the spreadsheet tutorial itself into proof of a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: We actually have a couple other ones that we actually make passive income through too as well
Things that we're actually investing in, me and my team are actually investing in, is what we actually post on there.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The spreadsheet format does not make its assumptions reliable or educationally neutral. The demonstration is used to produce a specific claim that the viewer recovers the investment in roughly three to four months, followed by an unequivocal endorsement. The separate paid-group invitation confirms that the tutorial is part of a promotional funnel, rather than a detached technical lesson.

citations.quote: Pretty much the entire point of the video is that you get your money back in literally 3.3 months, 3.6 months, 3.whatever months is where you make it back.
So is StrongBlock worth it? Yes, absolutely.
click the link down below join our team only crypto fans

opening.argument: The material can be understood as promotion of an ordinary paid information service alongside discussion of a crypto product, not evidence of a fraudulent deposit scheme. The speaker describes a subscription period, says the team conducts research for members, and presents its offer as access to investment ideas. He also states that the offer includes a money-back guarantee. The supplied evidence does not show a request for wallet credentials, a downline, or a requirement that viewers recruit others. Nor does the spreadsheet view establish that money is transferred to the presenter; it shows a calculator and an instruction to make a copy in order to edit it.

citations.quote: we only are giving to97 during the annual subscription period
a team of hustlers that realistically we're doing the research for you
you have 100 money back guarantee

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of a paid service and a refund statement supports ordinary commerce: customers are offered research access, not asked to surrender credentials or recruit a network. The node discussion identifies a service fee and a token-based output, but the supplied material does not establish that the presenter controls viewers' funds or that payment guarantees the claimed return. Those missing elements matter when distinguishing a questionable investment pitch from a demonstrated scam mechanism.

citations.quote: click the link down below join our team only crypto fans
you have 100 money back guarantee
pay your node fees 20 bucks per note

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The paid-group offer is not the only issue. The speaker directly promotes StrongBlock as an investment, calculates recovery of the initial outlay, and tells viewers it is worthwhile. A money-back statement for the separate group does not protect viewers from losses in the node investment, and the absence of credential theft or recruitment does not negate a paid node-return claim.
